ollama.label: Ollama local setup
ollama.placeholder: No API key needed for Ollama

ollama.guidance: Local Ollama mode is experimental. It keeps requests on your computer, but the feedback can be slower, shorter, or less useful than Gemini, OpenAI, or Mistral. By default, Career Signal uses a mixed local strategy with Gemma 4 first and Qwen 3.6 as a fallback. You can choose one model manually if you prefer.
ollama.analysisGuidance: Generating a full reconstruction plan with Ollama can take several minutes and may be less reliable than cloud models. For the fastest full plan, use Gemini, OpenAI, or Mistral.
ollama.timeoutMessage: The local Ollama model took too long to answer this section. Try again, choose a smaller local model, or use Gemini, OpenAI, or Mistral for a more reliable reconstruction plan.
ollama.customGuidance: Use this only for a model you already installed in Ollama. The app will send the typed model name to your local Ollama server.

modelCommands.local-mix: Install both models if you want fallback: ollama run gemma4, then ollama run qwen3.6.

feedback.cvInputGuidance: First add the source CV. The app checks whether there is enough evidence before it rewrites anything for a target job.
feedback.ageWarning: Your study year may reveal more age related information than necessary. For many private sector CVs, especially after several years of experience, it may be better to keep relevant studies but remove completion years or older education details. This is only a warning. You can keep the year if you want.
feedback.allExperienceWarning: Including all experiences may make the CV too long or reveal unnecessary historical information. Use this only if the older experience is highly relevant to the target role.

feedback.acknowledgeStudyWarning: Acknowledge the study-year privacy warning before continuing.

tailoring.guidanceLocked: You can add the target company and job description now. Generation unlocks after the CV evidence precheck, or after you explicitly choose to continue despite a weak precheck.
tailoring.guidanceUnlocked: Use the target company and job description to generate a reconstruction plan grounded in the CV evidence already checked above. You can test multiple target roles without rerunning the precheck as long as the CV and profile details stay the same.
tailoring.initialLock: Run the CV Evidence Precheck first. This keeps the tailoring step from polishing weak or unsupported claims.
tailoring.staleLock: The CV or profile details changed after the last precheck. Run the precheck again before tailoring.
tailoring.weakLock: The precheck recommends improving the CV first. Choose Continue anyway below to unlock generation.
tailoring.reviewLock: Review the precheck result, then choose Continue to Job Tailoring below to unlock generation.
tailoring.weakUnlock: Unlocked because you chose to continue despite the weak CV warning.

weakCvWarning: This CV appears to contain mostly descriptions of responsibilities rather than measurable results. Tailoring it to a job description now may produce a better looking document, but it will not solve the core problem. Add concrete outcomes and numerical evidence first.

evidenceRecovery.title: Evidence recovery examples
evidenceRecovery.intro: These are prompts to help recover truthful evidence from the CV. They are not final CV wording.
evidenceRecovery.guardrail: Do not paste these examples as-is. Replace every bracketed idea with something true, defensible, and specific to your work.
evidenceRecovery.noWeakExamples: No specific weak line was detected, so use the generic recovery pattern below.
evidenceRecovery.genericSubjects: people, clients, teams, services, cases, systems, documents, or operations
evidenceRecovery.genericOutcomes: quality, safety, speed, cost, satisfaction, reliability, compliance, risk, continuity, or adoption
evidenceRecovery.summaryPattern: {role} with experience supporting {subjects}. Contributed to work where the strongest evidence to recover is {outcomes}, using truthful numbers, timeframes, and scope.
evidenceRecovery.afterPattern: Try recovering: {activity} for [number] {subjects} across [timeframe/context], helping improve [specific {outcomes}] by [number/result if true].
defaultMissingEvidence: Volume or scale: how many people, cases, clients, users, systems, documents, shifts, or services were affected.
Timeframe: how long the work took, how often it happened, or how quickly something improved.
Outcome: what changed in quality, safety, cost, speed, satisfaction, reliability, compliance, risk, continuity, or adoption.
Ownership: what you personally delivered, influenced, coordinated, or supported.
defaultQuestions: What changed because of this work?
How many people, cases, clients, users, systems, documents, shifts, or services were involved?
What was better after the work: quality, safety, speed, cost, satisfaction, reliability, compliance, risk, continuity, or adoption?
What number, timeframe, baseline, or comparison can you defend in an interview?

healthcare.subjects: patients, shifts, care activities, records, families, teams, units, or services
healthcare.outcomes: patient safety, response time, continuity of care, documentation quality, patient flow, satisfaction, or risk reduction

education.subjects: students, learners, classes, training sessions, curricula, teams, or learning programs
education.outcomes: learning progress, participation, completion, satisfaction, assessment quality, adoption, or support coverage

customer.subjects: customers, clients, accounts, cases, opportunities, regions, products, or service requests
customer.outcomes: revenue, retention, satisfaction, response time, conversion, pipeline quality, risk reduction, or service quality

technology.subjects: users, systems, applications, platforms, environments, teams, processes, or data flows
technology.outcomes: cost, reliability, speed, adoption, security, automation, quality, risk reduction, or delivery time

operations.subjects: processes, services, cases, teams, sites, suppliers, documents, inventories, or workflows
operations.outcomes: quality, speed, cost, compliance, safety, reliability, throughput, risk reduction, or service continuity

personalDataWarnings.title: Privacy and bias risk review
personalDataWarnings.intro: The CV appears to include personal details that may be unnecessary or risky in many hiring processes. This is a practical warning, not a legal decision. Keep these details only when the target country, sector, or employer explicitly requires them.

jobFitAssessment.warningFallback: This is an evidence-based estimate, not a hiring decision. The final decision always belongs to the company and may depend on interviews, internal priorities, competition, timing, compensation, legal requirements, and information not present here.

appHelp.title: Career Signal guide
appHelp.subtitle: Simple help, privacy, scoring, and limits in one place.

blocks.title: In simple words
blocks.text: Career Signal checks whether your CV has enough real evidence before helping you tailor it to a job.

blocks.title: Basic flow
items: Add your years of experience and choose whether studies are listed.
Upload a CV PDF, LinkedIn PDF export, or paste your CV text.

Choose OpenRouter, OpenAI, Gemini, Mistral, Claude (experimental), DeepSeek, or Ollama (offline, experimental), then choose a model. OpenRouter’s listed models are free; custom OpenRouter model IDs may be paid depending on your OpenRouter account.
For cloud providers, add a key if it is not already configured.
For Ollama, install Ollama locally, download the selected model, and keep Ollama running.
Run the CV Evidence Precheck first.
If the CV has enough evidence, add the target company, optional company context, and the job description.
Generate the reconstruction plan and review it before using anything.

blocks.title: About provider keys
blocks.text: If the backend already has provider keys configured, you can leave the key field empty. If not, paste your own provider key for that request. Career Signal does not store the key; it is sent only to the backend you are using so the selected AI provider can process the CV check.

blocks.title: Important habit
blocks.text: Use the output as a review and rewriting assistant. Confirm every title, date, employer, tool, metric, and claim before sending a CV.

blocks.title: CV Evidence Precheck
blocks.text: The precheck score is 0 to 100. It estimates whether the CV contains enough defensible evidence to tailor safely.

blocks.title: What it looks for
items: Concrete outcomes, not only responsibilities.
Numbers, scale, scope, dates, users, systems, budgets, teams, risks, or measurable changes when they are true.
Bullets that explain what changed because of the work.
Warnings about unsupported claims, sensitive personal details, confusing titles, unclear progression, tense problems, and unnecessary education details.
Questions that help recover missing metrics without inventing anything.

blocks.title: Profile match assessment
blocks.text: After the precheck, the job-specific profile match score is also 0 to 100. It estimates how strongly the provided CV evidence matches the target role and company context.

blocks.title: What the numbers mean
items: A high score means the evidence looks stronger, clearer, and more relevant.
A medium score means the CV may be usable but needs clarification, better proof, or stronger targeting.
A low score means tailoring may make the CV look better without solving the evidence problem.
No score guarantees interviews, hiring outcomes, or recruiter decisions.

blocks.title: What it does
items: Checks whether a CV has enough evidence before tailoring.
Highlights weak or risky areas before they become polished but unsupported claims.
Uses a target company and job description to produce a job-specific reconstruction plan.
Helps identify keywords, matching evidence, missing signals, recruiter interpretation, and integrity risks.
Encourages safer CV writing by warning about age, gender, citizenship, photo, address, and other personal details when they are unnecessary.

blocks.title: What it does not do
items: It does not invent achievements, metrics, employers, dates, tools, certifications, or responsibilities.
It does not apply to jobs automatically.
It does not guarantee interviews or hiring outcomes.
It does not replace the final judgment of a recruiter, hiring manager, or company.
It does not replace your responsibility to check the final CV before sending it.

blocks.title: What the app stores
items: The app does not store CVs in a database.
The app does not store API keys.
The app does not add analytics or tracking to the core CV workflow.
Your pasted key is sent only to the local backend for that request.

blocks.title: What leaves your machine
items: If you run an AI check, the CV text and job details are sent to the AI provider you selected.
If you use OpenRouter, the request goes to OpenRouter with the selected free model.
If you use Gemini, the request goes to Google with the selected Gemini model.
If you use DeepSeek, the request goes to DeepSeek with the selected DeepSeek model.
If you use OpenAI, the request goes to OpenAI with the selected OpenAI model.
If you use Mistral, the request goes to Mistral with the selected Mistral model.
If you use Claude (experimental), the request goes to Anthropic with the selected Claude model.
If you use Ollama (offline, experimental), the backend sends the request to your configured local Ollama URL instead of a cloud AI provider.
The Buy Me a Coffee button is an external support widget and may load assets from Buy Me a Coffee or its CDN.

blocks.title: Open source
blocks.text: The project is fully open source under the GPL-3.0 license, so people can inspect, run, improve, and suggest changes.

blocks.title: About the creator
blocks.text: Career Signal was created by Federico Navarrete, a technologist, author, speaker, and open-source contributor based in Luxembourg.

blocks.title: Why this exists
blocks.text: The project helps people review CVs more critically before tailoring them to a role. It focuses on evidence, clarity, risk, and relevance without replacing human judgment.

cvBasics.title: High impact CV basics
cvBasics.subtitle: A strong CV makes real evidence easy to see.

blocks.title: What strong bullets prove
items: What changed because of your work.
Who or what was affected: users, clients, systems, teams, countries, budgets, risks, or processes.
The scale of the work and why it mattered.
The result: saved time, reduced cost, improved reliability, increased adoption, lowered risk, delivered migration, or supported decisions.

blocks.title: Weak activity language
items: Responsible for training teams.
Introduced governance framework.
Supported stakeholders.
Implemented process improvements.
Participated in projects.

blocks.title: Stronger evidence pattern
blocks.text: Use action, object, scale, purpose, and result. The bullet should survive the question: so what?
examples: Stronger: Supported approximately 200 to 300 people per day during peak COVID operations, maintaining patient flow under high pressure conditions.

blocks.title: Evidence-backed language
items: Personal claims such as motivated, efficient, strategic, reliable, or strong communicator should be supported by evidence.
The problem is not the adjective; the problem is when there is no proof nearby.
Replace unsupported self-description with outcomes, examples, scale, decisions, delivery, adoption, or measurable results.

blocks.title: Summary as an elevator pitch
items: Use the summary to explain what you bring to the role before the recruiter, hiring manager, or screening model reads the details.
Keep it short, concrete, and evidence-led: target role, strongest domain, relevant scale, and one or two standout outcomes.
If multilingual ability is a useful market signal, include it naturally in the summary with the business context it supports.
Avoid generic claims such as results-driven or passionate unless the summary immediately proves them with scope, results, or rare strengths.
examples: Cloud transformation engineer fluent in English, French, and German; reduced AWS waste by 40% in test environments and helped European stakeholders align migration, automation, and cost-governance decisions.

blocks.title: Languages and market signal
items: List languages clearly and truthfully, using practical levels such as English - fluent, French - professional, or German - conversational.
If multilingual ability is relevant to the role, market, clients, or region, mention it in the summary or intro instead of hiding it at the end.
Do not assume a language mix is ordinary everywhere. For example, an engineer who can work in English, French, and German has a rare cross-border signal in many European markets.
Prioritize languages that support the target role, company, country, client base, or stakeholder environment.

blocks.title: Tense and timing
items: Use past tense for completed work, especially in previous roles.
Use present tense only for responsibilities or work that is genuinely still ongoing.
For current roles, completed achievements should still read as completed outcomes, not as open-ended activity.
Avoid infinitive-style bullets when the achievement already happened.

blocks.title: Before tailoring
items: Recover numbers where they are true and defensible.
Remove or de-emphasize old details that do not help the target role.

Keep studies and credentials only when relevant or required. Avoid listing graduation years once you have several years of professional experience (typically around five years), as they can unnecessarily introduce age bias. Exceptions may include PhDs, degrees from highly prestigious (international) universities, or school diplomas only for recent graduates.
Never invent metrics, tools, responsibilities, employers, dates, certifications, or achievements.

blocks.title: Length by seniority
items: Junior or early-career CVs are usually strongest at 1 page.
Mid-career CVs are usually 1 to 2 pages.
Senior specialists, managers, or consultants usually need around 2 pages.
Executives, academics, researchers, public sector profiles, or highly credentialed experts may need more when the extra detail is relevant.
Length is not bad by itself; the problem is when it hides the strongest evidence or removes proof that should be visible.

blocks.title: Long tenure and progression
items: Long tenure is not a problem by itself, but one title covering many years can make growth look flat.
If you held multiple internal positions, show the real sequence instead of only the latest title.
If formal titles did not change, show scope progression through truthful bullets: larger teams, bigger budgets, broader regions, harder systems, or higher-impact work.

blocks.title: Title and responsibility alignment
items: Make sure each official title matches the responsibilities and accomplishments listed below it.
If the title is Project Manager but the bullets describe product ownership, architecture, strategy, training, or operations, clarify the scope instead of letting the reader guess.
Hybrid roles are fine, but unusual scope should be explained with truthful wording such as a role subtitle, scope line, or clear bullet context.

blocks.title: Sensitive personal details
items: Avoid date of birth, exact age, marital status, family status, gender, citizenship, nationality, full home address, or photo references unless they are explicitly required.
Use location only at the useful level for the role, such as city, country, or work authorization when relevant.
These details can create privacy, discrimination, or age-bias risk and usually do not strengthen the evidence of impact.

blocks.title: References
items: Do not include references or referee contact details by default.
Use references available upon request only when it is expected in the target country, sector, or application form.
Protect other people’s privacy: share names, phone numbers, emails, or direct recommendations only when requested and when the referee has agreed.

blocks.title: Contact basics
items: Put name, email, phone, and useful location near the top.
Add LinkedIn or portfolio when it helps prove the profile.
Missing contact details are uncommon, but they create unnecessary friction for recruiters.
